title: SCPE scpe/0.1 manifest.json
description: Structural shape of an SCPE scpe/0.1 manifest.json (SPEC.md §4). Derived from SPEC.md and the eighteen manifests under spec/test-vectors/*/manifest.json.
$comment: DESCRIPTIVE / ADVISORY ONLY. The normative check for what makes a manifest valid is SPEC.md §8 (the verification algorithm) plus the reference/impl verifiers, not this file. This schema deliberately does NOT enforce several things SPEC.md treats as verification-time (not parse-time) failures, so that manifests which are structurally well-formed but semantically rejected by a verifier still validate here — several test vectors are exactly that on purpose: unsupported-provider (contributor.identity.provider = 'oidc', a reserved-but-not-implemented provider, §11.1), unsupported-subject (subject.type = 'container-image', an unknown subject kind that fails closed per §6.3), identity-unverifiable-subject (contributor.identity.subject = 'evil..traversal', violates the §8 safe-subject rule), and unknown-version (spec_version = 'scpe/9.9', an unsupported MAJOR per §11). This schema intentionally leaves provider, subject.type, subject.identity.subject's charset, and spec_version's MAJOR unconstrained (beyond basic string/pattern shape) for that reason. It also does not restrict additional properties anywhere, per §11's forward-compatibility rule that verifiers MUST accept an unknown MINOR's new optional fields. Validate a manifest against this schema to catch structural typos early; then run an actual SPEC §8 verifier for the real answer.

spec_version.description: scpe/<MAJOR>.<MINOR> (§11). This schema only checks the string shape. An unknown MAJOR (e.g. 'scpe/9.9' — see spec/test-vectors/unknown-version) is still structurally valid JSON and validates here; §8 step 2 is what rejects it as unsupported-version at verification time.

provider.description: Key-resolution method (§8, §11.1), read by the verifier at §8 step 3. scpe/0.1 implements exactly four: github, gitlab, codeberg, local. Not restricted to an enum here: the registry is a closed set enforced by the VERIFIER (fail-safe: unsupported-provider), not a schema-level constraint — a manifest naming a reserved-but-unimplemented or future provider (e.g. 'oidc', see spec/test-vectors/unsupported-provider) is still a structurally valid manifest and validates here.

subject.description: Username within `provider` — the forge identity the signature is checked against (§8 steps 3-6). The §8 safe-subject rule (^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9._-]{0,63}$, and no '..' substring) is a verification-time check (failure -> identity-unverifiable), not enforced here, so a subject that violates it (e.g. 'evil..traversal', see spec/test-vectors/identity-unverifiable-subject) still validates structurally.

key_fingerprint.description: SHA256 fingerprint of the signing key, e.g. 'SHA256:<base64>' (§4).

type.description: Discriminator read by the verifier's integrity step (§8 step 7, §6.3). scpe/0.1 implements 'code-change' (§6.1) and 'artifact' (§6.2, standalone-only); any other value is a subject kind the reference verifier does not implement and fails closed to unsupported-subject rather than being a schema error — see spec/test-vectors/unsupported-subject (type 'container-image').

repo.description: owner/name or URL of the repository the diff applies to (§6.1).

base_sha.description: Full commit SHA the diff applies to (§6.1).

diff_sha256.description: The code-change integrity anchor (§6.1): SHA-256 hex over the normalized diff.patch bytes. This is the exact field the verifier's integrity step (§8 step 7) recomputes and compares; a mismatch is 'tampered' (see spec/test-vectors/tampered-diff).

head_sha.description: The exact commit the contributor produced. Informational (§6.1) — recorded for audit, not part of the integrity check, and breaks under rebase by design.

sha256.description: The artifact integrity anchor (§6.2): SHA-256 hex over the raw artifact bytes (no normalization). The field the verifier's integrity step (§8 step 7) compares against the hashed enclosed artifact.bin; a mismatch is 'tampered' (see spec/test-vectors/tampered-artifact).

media_type.description: SHOULD (§6.2) — the artifact's MIME type; informational, not verified.

profile.description: Optional domain-convention label (§4, §13). Registry (§13.1): SCPE-C, SCPE-I, SCPE-V, SCPE-A, SCPE-M, SCPE-DATA, SCPE-D, SCPE-AR. Purely advisory: the verifier surfaces it verbatim and NEVER dispatches on it for the verdict (§13.2), and an unregistered value is surfaced-but-ignored, never an error — so this schema does not restrict the string to the registry list.

attestations.description: Optional list of typed, signed claims (§5). Omitted or [] means none.

type.description: Attestation discriminator (§5.1) read by the verifier's per-entry summary (§5.3, §8 step 8). Registered in scpe/0.1: 'agent-trace' (implemented), 'timestamp' and 'countersignature' (reserved, format-only, reported present-unverified). Any other value is likewise an unknown type -> present-unverified, never an error, never a silent pass -- still a structurally valid entry.

format.description: Selects the payload shape within `type` (§5.2, used by 'agent-trace': 'agent-trace/1', 'git-ai/notes', 'generic/1'). Every registered type in scpe/0.1 carries `format`, but it is optional in this schema so a future `type` without one still validates -- see the unknown-type fail-safe, §5.3.

data.description: Type/format-specific payload (§5.2 for agent-trace; opaque for reserved types).

extensions.description: Optional free-form map (§4). Verifiers MUST ignore unknown keys.
